name: SCHWIMMEN
description: Schwimmen (31) is a Commerce-group card game in which players hold three cards and improve their hand by exchanging with a central pool of three face-up cards. The aim is to collect cards of one suit totalling as high as possible (maximum 31) or three of a kind. Played with chips; the loser of each hand loses a chip and the last survivor wins. Popular in Germany and Austria.

Country/Region of Origin: Austria and Germany (particularly western Austria and Germany). Known in many parts of the world.
Time Period: Early 1900s
Historical Development: The game evolved from traditional card games in the region; German name Schwimmen (swimming) refers to the last chance before a player drops out.
Cultural Significance: Popular social and family game in Austria and Germany

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: Optional

Type: 32-card deck (strip 2-6 from standard pack). Cards 7-10, J, Q, K, A in four suits. One deck.
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included

32-card deck (or strip 2-6 from standard deck)
Chips or tokens (e.g. 3 per player)
Table space

Dealer gives 3 cards face down to each player plus one extra hand of 3 cards. Dealer chooses to keep their own 3 or the extra hand (before seeing the extra hand). The rejected 3 cards are turned face up and placed in the centre as the table pool. Dealing pattern: clockwise.

items.text: Dutch 31: You must exchange or close each turn (no pass). Closing does not end the hand; play continues until only two remain, then one may close. Declaring 31 ends the hand immediately. No Feuer; three aces score 30.5. Often scored with dice (start at 6); first to 0 gets the Chicken (one extra life).

41: Four cards each and four face-up on table (52-card pack); max hand value 41. Options: swap one card, swap all four, replace table and then swap one, or end the game. Winner gains points equal to hand value; losers lose the difference. Ties with winner also win.
